doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The 1953 recordings issued on CD and the concert music year
summary: Teo Macero helped him edit raw tapes for CBS, leading to two CDs, with the quintet and a year of concert works (Berezowsky, Mozart, Brahms).

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: This is what turned out to be these two CDs. Then I got another collection together of that same material, that went to Book-of-the-Month. I was going to play you, and I will later play you, a couple of records of that that I was talking to you about.
Yeah. That quintet. Again, that was . . . no, that was before I went to Spain. After I tried playing just concert music for a year . . .

. . . playing long-form music. The Berezowsky [Nicolai Berezowsky]. De la Joya [?who] did a concerto. And I did the Mozart and the Brahms quintet, and the Mozart quintet, and all of that. I’m going to put out the Mozart quintet and the Berezowsky concerto, which are all on that Legacy album. That’s what I’m going to do. At that time, that’s what I was doing. Getting stuff together, and meanwhile writing. Writing, writing, writing. That’s what I did. I worked at writing like I used to at music.
